rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both proclamations follow the same detailed escape-clause sequence: establish the GATT schedules and prevailing concessions; identify the affected tariff items and current treatment; recite a Tariff Commission investigation finding increased imports and serious injury; determine that modified concessions and new customs treatment are necessary; invoke section 350, section 7(c), and Article XIX; then modify the schedule and direct application of the modified item while suspending inconsistent prior proclamations. The child's operative paragraph (b) is especially close to C07's corresponding provision. C04 and C10 share much of the same escape-clause machinery, but C07 is materially closer in language, schedule treatment, and operative organization.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the United States Tariff Commission has submitted to me a report of its Investigation No. 7-101 under section 7 ... on the basis of which investigation, and a hearing held in connection therewith, the Commission has found that, as a result in part of the duties reflecting the concessions ... [the products are] being imported ... in such increased quantities, both actual and relative, as to cause serious injury
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the United States Tariff Commission ... submitted to me a report ... of its investigation No. 61 under section 7 ... on the basis of which investigation, and a hearing held in connection therewith, the Commission has found that, as a result in part of the duties reflecting the concessions ... [the products] were being imported ... in such increased quantities, both actual and relative, as to cause serious injury
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive, extended parallel language describes the same investigation, causal finding, and serious-injury predicate, with only the investigation number and product changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: acting under the authority vested in me by section 350 ... and by section 7(c) ... and in accordance with the provisions of Article XIX ... do proclaim that, effective after the close of business April 18, 1962, and until the President otherwise proclaims
shared_material.parent_excerpt: acting under the authority vested in me by section 350 ... and by section 7(c) ... and in accordance with the provisions of Article XIX ... do proclaim that, effective November 1, 1959, and until the President otherwise proclaims
shared_material.explanation: The authority clause and indefinite-duration formulation are substantially identical and perform the same function.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The descriptions of products in the said item 219 in Part I of Schedule XX-1956 and the pertinent rates ... are hereby modified
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the said prevailing tariff concessions ... are hereby modified by adding the following proviso at the end of item 339 in Part I of Schedule XX-1956
shared_material.explanation: Both directly amend a specified item in Part I of Schedule XX-1956 to impose the adjusted treatment.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the provisions of item 219 in Part I of Schedule XX-1956, as modified by (a) above, shall be applied and all inconsistent provisions of proclamations of the President heretofore issued under the authority of section 350 ... are suspended
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The provisions of the proviso to item 339 in Part I of Schedule XX-1956, added by paragraph (a) above, shall be applied and all proclamations of the President heretofore issued under the authority of section 350 ... are suspended insofar as they are inconsistent with this proclamation
shared_material.explanation: This is a highly specific near-verbatim operative mechanism linking application of the amended schedule item with suspension of inconsistent prior proclamations.
